column2: Your understanding of all matters of rulership and administration has grown. Ledgers that once swam before your eyes now tell you plainly where the gold goes, and who is taking it.
Recent judgements have sharpened your grasp of stewardship.
Ruling from your court has sharpened your sense of justice. Your judgements change the lives of your subjects, and you have resolved to make them fair.
As more and more petitioners seek an audience, you have come to see how much there is to do in the running of the realm. You must work harder!
You are no longer content to rest on your laurels. The troubles of your realm are legion, and clearly no one can fix them but you.

Whether it is deserved or not, your judgements have earned you a name for great wisdom. Petitioners travel from far beyond your borders to seek your counsel, and your words are repeated in taverns you will never see.
Your vassals have come to respect your rule, even when they do not agree with your decisions. No one questions that you have what it takes to rule.

An architect has been brought before your court with a proposal. With your blessing he will raise a new castle in [castle_site.GetName]. His design is novel, he says, and will need far less stone and gold than such a work normally demands, without giving up an inch of its strength. Your [Root.GetTreasurerName] has no opinion of the man, and you must judge him yourself.

An architect has been brought before your court, offering to raise a new castle in [castle_site.GetName] for far less than such a work normally costs. Before you can answer, [Root.job_treasurer.GetFullName], your [Root.GetTreasurerName], leans close and whispers: 'I know this one. He built the new walls at [Root.Capital.GetName] for my old master, and they have not cracked yet. We can trust him.'

An architect has been brought before your court, offering to raise a new castle in [castle_site.GetName] for far less than such a work normally costs. Before you can answer, [Root.job_treasurer.GetFullName], your [Root.GetTreasurerName], leans close and whispers: 'This charlatan is known to me. Half the debtors' prisons between here and Tilea have his name on the wall. He cannot be trusted.'
Build the castle!
No, we have no need of his services.

Your guards caught the architect you hired to build your castle in [castle_site.GetName] trying to slip away with the gold. The wretch had already spent much of it on drink and worse, but the rest has been returned to your coffers. It seems there will be no castle.
To the dungeons with him!

The building of your new castle in [castle_site.GetName] has been plagued by delays, stolen timber and quarries that ran dry. It seems the architect's first reckoning of the cost was somewhat... hopeful. More gold is needed if the castle is ever to be finished.
Confound it all! Give them the gold they need.
Abandon the work. Let us save what we can.
The castle you commissioned in [castle_site.GetName] has been finished, and it needed even less than was promised! The surplus stone and timber have been sold and the gold returned to your coffers.
Excellent!
The castle you commissioned in [castle_site.GetName] has been finished more or less on time, and its walls look sturdy enough to hold against anything short of a Dawi cannon.
Not bad.
The castle you commissioned in [castle_site.GetName] is finally finished. Despite all the setbacks, its walls look sturdy.
About time.
There is no longer any place in your demesne for the castle you commissioned, and the work has stopped. Fortunately, most of the gold had not yet been spent.
Ah, that's right... they were building a castle there.

A peasant accused of murder is dragged before your court. His wife and children were found butchered in their hut, and he was standing over them, red to the elbows. He swears by every god he knows that he came home to find them so, and that he saw something pale and many-limbed flee into the woods. What should be done with him?
This animal must hang.
Throw him in the dungeons and leave him there.
The evidence is thin. Let him go.
Perhaps some torture will loosen his tongue.

Your guards report that another peasant family has been found butchered not far from the first. This time the killer was caught at the work, a gibbering mutant with too many joints in its arms, and it was shot full of arrows when it tried to flee. It seems the peasant you hanged was telling the truth after all...
Perhaps my verdict was a little... hasty.

Your guards report that another peasant family has been found butchered not far from the first. This time the killer was caught at the work: the very peasant you set free. He was shot full of arrows when he tried to flee, still laughing.
It was probably a bad idea to let him go.
The peasant confessed under torture. Unfortunately, he expired in the process, so you may never learn what drove such a beast to murder his own family. Oh well.
Justice has been served. Probably.
Despite everything your torturers could think of, the peasant refused to confess. Unfortunately, he expired in the process, but surely it was only a matter of time before he told the truth...?
Yes... yes, of course.

Another peasant family has been found butchered not far from the first, and this time the killer was caught at the work: a mutant with too many joints in its arms, hiding in the woods. The guards killed it as it fled, and whatever it was, it was decidedly not the peasant who died in your torture chamber.
Well... fancy that.

Your guards report that another peasant family has been found butchered not far from the first. This time the killer was caught at the work, a mutant hiding in the woods, and it was shot full of arrows when it tried to flee. It seems the peasant in your dungeon was innocent after all.
Well, don't just stand there! Set him free!

Your guards report that another peasant family has been found butchered not far from the first. This time the killer was caught at the work, a mutant hiding in the woods, and it was shot full of arrows when it tried to flee. It seems the peasant in your dungeon was innocent after all. Unfortunately, he died down there months ago.
Well, how was I to know?

Another day at court, and another endless procession of matters you must judge. As yet another peasant drones on about his sickly pigs and the neighbour he is sure poisoned them, a great emptiness opens inside you. This is not the life you imagined.

Another day on the throne, and another endless line of grumbling underlings who want you to settle their squabbles. As yet another one whines about his stolen beasts and the rival who took them, a great emptiness opens inside you. This is not the life you imagined.
By [This.Religion.GetRandomGodName], will you shut up about your pigs?!

No matter how many matters you settle, there are always more. As the din of quarrelling nobles fills your hall, something in you snaps, and you shove your way through the startled crowd towards the door.
I can't take this anymore.

The feud between [feuding_noble_1.GetBestName] and [feuding_noble_2.GetBestName] has reached your court and can no longer be ignored. Burnt hay-ricks, stolen cattle, a cousin found in a ditch: each blames the other, and both have come to you hoping for your support.
[feuding_noble_1.GetTitledFirstName] is clearly in the right.
[feuding_noble_2.GetTitledFirstName] has my support.
Both of you are acting like quarrelling children!

A company of soldiers under the banner of [farm_fire_noble.GetBestName] recently camped in a farmer's field in [Root.Capital.GetName]. Their cookfires got away from them, and the whole crop went up in smoke. The farmer has come before your court demanding compensation.
[farm_fire_noble.GetTitledFirstName] will compensate the farmer.
The fire was an act of the gods. No one is responsible.
I will pay the farmer out of my own coffers.

Several tavern keepers from [drunken_rampage.GetName] have come to your court with complaints against [noble_drunkard.GetBestName]. It seems [noble_drunkard.GetSheHe] has gone on drunken rampages through every one of their houses, and they want to be paid for the broken benches, barrels and heads. [noble_drunkard.GetTitledFirstName] claims to remember nothing of the nights in question.
[noble_drunkard.GetTitledFirstName] will compensate the tavern keepers.
Drinking and brawling are what taverns are for, are they not?
Sigh... I will pay.

During a visit to [mayor_city.GetName], [brigands_noble.GetBestName] and [brigands_noble.GetHerHis] retinue were set upon by footpads who made off with several valuables. The city watch has caught no one, and [brigands_noble.GetTitledFirstName] now demands compensation from [brigands_mayor.GetBestName]. The matter has been brought to your court.
It seems fair. [brigands_mayor.GetTitledFirstName] will pay for what was lost.
[brigands_mayor.GetTitledFirstName] can hardly be blamed for every cutpurse in the city!
I will compensate [brigands_noble.GetTitledFirstName] myself.

A woman accused of witchcraft in [witch_province.GetName] has been dragged before your court. Several witnesses swear they saw her muttering over strange fires by her lonely hut, and the crops have failed and the cows gone dry since. She claims she is innocent, and it falls to you to decide her fate.

A woman accused of witchcraft in [witch_province.GetName] has been dragged before your court in chains. A Witch Hunter's broadsheet is pinned to the door of her parish church, and the villagers swear they saw her muttering over strange fires on Geheimnisnacht, when both moons were full. The crops have failed since. She claims she is innocent, but the priests of Sigmar are watching to see what you will do.
She will burn at the stake.
Throw the witch in the dungeons!
What nonsense is this? Release the poor woman at once!
Shallya's Almoner
This character rules as Shallya teaches: the granaries are open, the hospices are full, and the poor of the realm bless their name.
